==Background==
The Southern California Gas Company (SoCalGas), a subsidiary of Sempra<ref name=":2" /> operates the SoCalGas pipeline which runs from Visalia in Tulare County all the way down to the Mexican border. The genesis of the company began in 1867 as the Los Angeles Gas Company which installed gas lamps. In 1890, it was bought by Pacific Lightning later becoming SoCalGas. The demise of gas lamps led SoCalGas to seek other opportunities and in the 1940s, they began building pipelines amidst the discovery of natural gas and the growing demand for fuel. Today, the pipeline serves 19.5 million people<ref name=":3" />. 

===Adelanto Lateral===
The U.S. Energy Information Administration lists the project as an expansion completed in February 2002. It lists the line as intrastate and regulated by the state.<ref name="r30800f" />

== Accidents ==
In October 23, 2015, there was a gas leak from the Aliso Canyon gas storage causing 10,000 families of Porter Ranch, Chatsworth, Northridge and Granada Hills to evacuate<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weitzlux.com/environmental/pollution/porter-ranch-aliso-canyon-california-gas-leak/|title=Aliso Canyon Gas Leak Lawsuits {{!}} Porter Ranch, California|website=Weitz & Luxenberg|language=en-US|access-date=2024-04-11}}</ref>. In an on-going UCLA study it is reported that the leak released 100,000 metric tons of methane<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://alisostudy.ucla.edu/|title=Aliso Canyon Disaster Health Research Study|last=admin|website=UCLA Aliso Canyon Disaster Health Research Study|language=en|access-date=2024-04-11}}</ref>, which according to the Environmental Defense Fund is the same as GHG emissions from 7 million cars or 9 coal fired plants<ref name=":3" />.  It is the largest uncontrolled release of methane from an underground gas storage facility in the US and the "worst environmental disaster since the Deep Horizon oil spill"<ref name=":3" />. It took 4 months for the leak to be sealed. SoCalGas agreed to a $71 million settlement in 2023<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/socalgas-to-pay-71-million-in-settlement-with-cpuc-over-aliso-canyon-gas-blowout/3204075/|title=SoCalGas to pay $71 million in settlement with CPUC over Aliso Canyon gas blowout|last=Service • •|first=City News|date=2023-08-11|website=NBC Los Angeles|language=en-US|access-date=2024-04-11}}</ref>. Residents thought the settlement would close the plant however, the California Public Utilities Commission voted to expand the plant.
